observed: A session searched the family with shell invocations (rg over F:/Documents and the driver checkout) instead of the family's own probes, and treated CUA as a capture/measurement helper rather than the machine driver whose declared tools (fs.search, fs.read, shell.exec, screen.capture, test.run) own system, code and kernel-level work. The owner corrected both: "why are you using shell searches instead of probes that use family evidence to search across the entire system" and "never use a shell search again the cua machine drivers will handle it eventually this is a family wide harness requirement", after "this is not a request. You are not conforming to the family yourself as an external agent working within it's surfaces and security systems." The two terminal readings immediately before the ruling returned an unknown local outcome, so the walk was also unverifiable. The ruling is family-wide, not this project's preference.
correction: No shell search (rg, grep -r, find, piped ls, xargs over a file list) in any family project. Evidence is asked for through tools/family_failures.py (ledger sweep, serve/probe over loopback), openlock_modern tools/family_search.py (family-wide documents and provenance receipt) and the editor search tools, and the CUA driver's declared tools take the query when fs.search is wired to the same roots. The look check that prompted this is to be expressed through the driver's registry and its ToolResult codes, not a pixel heuristic beside it. Recorded in docs/family-development-policy.md under 'No shell searches'.
